title: Indian Market News Brief — 01 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Strong earnings from major power and stock depository companies along with government funds released to states may support market sentiment. Proposals by the market regulator to simplify rules for foreign investors could also help sentiment. However, rising bad loans in gold finance firms and changes in fuel export duties present mixed signals for specific sectors.

stories.headline: केंद्र सरकार ने राज्य सरकारों को कर हस्तांतरण के रूप में 1,09,019 करोड़ रुपये जारी किए। आगामी त्योहारों के मौसम को देखते हुए और राज्यों को पूंजीगत खर्च में तेजी लाने तथा विकास एवं कल्याण से जुड़े व्यय के लिए धन उपलब्ध कराने के उद्देश्य से केंद्र सरकार ने कर हस्तांतरण की अग्रिम किस्त जारी की है
stories.summary:
The central government released 1,09,019 crore rupees as tax transfers to state governments.
This is an advance release done before the upcoming festival season.
The aim is to help states spend more on development and public welfare projects.
States can use these funds to speed up their spending on capital projects.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Higher spending by state governments may boost demand for construction materials and consumer products.

stories.headline: NTPC Q2 results 2026 brings good news of 1st interim dividend for investors! Check amount, record date, profit details
stories.summary:
NTPC reported a 38.7 percent year-on-year rise in quarterly profit to 7,029.56 crore rupees.
Quarterly revenue grew 21.2 percent to reach 54,269.95 crore rupees.
The company declared its first interim dividend for the current financial year.
The record date for the dividend payment is set for November 6.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong growth in quarterly profits and dividend payout may attract buyers to power and utility stocks.

stories.headline: CDSL Q2 results: Net profit jumps 24% YoY to Rs 173 crore, revenue up 24%
stories.summary:
CDSL reported a 24 percent increase in quarterly net profit to 173 crore rupees.
Total revenue for the quarter rose 23.7 percent to 395 crore rupees.
The company opened around 75 lakh new demat accounts during the period.
Total assets held under its custody crossed 89 lakh crore rupees.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Steady growth in account openings and profits shows healthy activity in stock market services.

stories.headline: Muthoot Finance Q2 cons profit jumps 36% YoY to Rs 3,278 crore
stories.summary:
Muthoot Finance reported a 36 percent rise in quarterly net profit to 3,278 crore rupees.
Total loan assets under management grew 42 percent to 2.09 lakh crore rupees.
However, bad loans as a percentage of total loans increased to 3.87 percent.
This is higher than the 2.28 percent reported in the previous quarter.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: Strong profit growth is positive, but the jump in unpaid loans may create worry about asset quality.

stories.headline: Petrol export duty cut to nil; diesel levy raised to ₹11.5 per litre
stories.summary:
The government reduced the export duty on petrol to zero rupees.
At the same time, the export duty on diesel was raised to 11.5 rupees per litre.
The revision follows recent changes in global energy prices.
The policy also aims to ensure sufficient fuel availability within the country.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: Removing tax on petrol exports helps refiners, but a higher tax on diesel exports may lower profits.

stories.headline: Sebi to release FII compliance consultation paper within weeks, says chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey
stories.summary:
SEBI will soon release a discussion paper on compliance rules for foreign investors.
The regulator aims to align Indian market rules with global standard practices.
This step comes after recent heavy selling by foreign institutional investors.
SEBI also plans to build a training network to strengthen independent directors.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Easier compliance rules may make it simpler for foreign funds to invest in Indian shares.

stories.headline: US bonds rally, sending yields to biggest monthly decline since 2023
stories.summary:
US government bond prices rose sharply, leading to lower interest yield rates.
The ten-year US bond yield recorded its largest monthly fall in almost three years.
Investors moved money into safe government bonds following a fall in US tech stocks.
Markets continue to expect an interest rate cut from the US central bank in December.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Lower returns on US bonds can encourage global investors to put more money into emerging markets like India.

stories.headline: Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty
stories.summary:
SEBI banned EKI Energy Services from the securities market for two months.
The managing director was banned for 12 months for wrong financial reporting.
The regulator found that company funds were diverted improperly.
A former chief financial officer was also restrained from entering the market.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: Regulatory action against a small company protects market integrity but does not impact large index shares.

stories.headline: IMD sees better November rain in key wheat-growing regions
stories.summary:
The weather office expects good rain in major wheat-growing areas during November.
Normal to above-normal rainfall is likely in parts of central and north-west India.
November is a key month for sowing major winter crops across the country.
Better rainfall improves soil moisture required for healthy crop growth.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Good crop sowing conditions can lower food prices and improve income in rural areas.

stories.headline: Amid price rise, Indian govt doubles weekly wheat auction quantity
stories.summary:
The government doubled its weekly wheat auction allocation to 1.99 lakh tonnes.
This measure was taken to control rising domestic prices of wheat.
However, the maximum buying limit allowed for each bidder remains unchanged.
Market experts express doubts about whether this change will lower prices quickly.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Increasing food supply helps control price rises, which supports overall consumer spending.
